title: Seasonal temperature contrasts did not identify a clear delayed response in Finnish moth thermal composition, 1993-2022
abstract: We tested a seasonal carry-over account for the fast thermal change of Finnish moth communities. We used 1,243 annual samples at 62 sites in 1993-2022, external European species scores, and monthly air temperature. Models included site and year effects, previous, current and future summer temperature, and winter temperature before and after sampling. The previous-minus-future summer slope for count weights was 0.156 CTI C per air C. Its nominal 95% interval was 0.029 to 0.283, but its interval after adjustment for four planned tests was -0.010 to 0.322. All four adjusted contrast intervals included zero. Winter point contrasts were near zero. The full presence sample gave a summer contrast of 0.025; a matched large-catch sample gave 0.071, or 0.068 after fixed-catch weighting. Thus sample selection limits an abundance-only account. Count estimates stayed positive across site-trend, climate-interpolation, period-omission and major-species-removal checks. These are dependent checks, not independent confirmation. The result gives suggestive evidence for a delayed summer link but does not identify survival, recruitment, dispersal or a share of the long-term tracking gap. The package includes reproducible code, source hashes, aggregate evidence and figures. External records remain outside the package.

display.caption: Seasonal slopes and four planned direction contrasts. Dark bars show nominal 95% intervals. Light bars show 98.75% intervals for the four planned contrasts. All four adjusted intervals include zero. Site and year effects are included.
Sample restriction changes the presence result. Count contrasts stay positive in model checks. These dependent checks do not replace the four planned tests and do not identify a causal mechanism.
